ABSTRACT  
To promote the consumption of renewables in ports, based on the transportation-energy coupling characteristics 
of ports, a nested bi-layer energy management and capacity allocation method of hybrid energy storage system 
(HESS) is proposed to coordinate the imbalance between hydrogen/ electricity supply and demand. First, to 
coordinate the imbalance between multi-energy supply and demand, a multi-energy load model based on traffic 
scheduling in ports is established to realize the demand-side management of load. Then, considering carbon 
emission costs of ports and degradation costs of HESS, a “ transportation-energy ” collaborative scheduling model 
is proposed with the goal of optimizing the daily operating costs of ports. Furthermore, a HESS capacity allo -
cation model is formulated with the goal of minimizing the annual operational life cycle cost of ports. Finally, to 
improve the accuracy and efficiency of solving the capacity allocation model, an improved model-pursuing 
sampling (MPS) algorithm based on the metamodel is presented. The simulation results based on port histori -
cal data show that, compared with the traditional scheduling method, the daily operating cost of the collabo -
rative scheduling method is reduced by 7.2 %. Compared with empirical capacity, under the optimal HESS 
capacity, the annual cost of the port is reduced by 8.2 %. The annualized cost of ports obtained under the 
improved MPS algorithm is lower.   
1. Introduction 
At present, seaports undertake most of the logistics transit in the 
world, while also leading to significant energy consumption and envi -
ronmental pollution [ 1 ]. Port equipment electrification and hydroge -
nation are an important means for port energy consumption 
transformation. It can improve the energy efficiency, reduce carbon 
emissions, and achieve sustainable transportation of ports [ 2 ]. In recent 
years, cold ironing technology has been rapidly developed [ 3 ]. At the 
same time, fixed transportation equipment such as quay cranes (QCs) 
have gradually realized electrification, and mobile equipment, such as 
container trucks, yard cranes (YCs), and rubber-tired gantry (RTG) 
cranes are also gradually becoming hydrogen powered [ 4 ]. With the 
electrification/hydrogen power of the key logistics equipment in port, 
the traffic scheduling of ports not only affects logistics operations but 
also determines changes in port energy consumption, forming the 
“ transportation- energy ” coupling characteristics of ports. 
Studies have shown that renewable energy will become the most 
important energy source for low-carbon or even zero carbon ports in the 
future [ 5 ]. In addition, if ports can realize the localized production and 
consumption of hydrogen energy through renewables, it can effectively 
utilize the efficient and clean advantages of hydrogen energy and reduce 
costs, further promoting clean energy consumption in ports. However, 
with the increase of the penetration rate of renewables in ports, the anti- 
peak regulation characteristics of renewables seriously influence the 
“ source ” and “ load ” balance of port energy, affecting the clean energy 
utilization of ports. Energy storage systems (ESSs) are an effective way

However, with the acceleration of the integration of port transportation 
and energy, port energy consumption is deeply influenced by logistics 
characteristics, which leads to greater challenges to the coordinated 
control of ESSs. 
The key to coordinating the supply and demand imbalance of 
hydrogen/electricity in ports through ESSs mainly includes two aspects: 
one is the coordination strategy of ESSs, and the other is the capacity 
allocation of ESSs. However, the relevant research on the application of 
ESSs in ports is not yet mature, and even in many aspects is still in the 
initial stage. 
The coordination strategy of ESS is a key issue in improving port 
energy efficiency, reducing carbon emissions, and promoting clean en -
ergy consumption. The main technical means in current research include 
improving the operation efficiency of port areas and adopting clean 
energy to replace traditional energy. At present, improving the 
operation efficiency of port areas is mainly achieved by optimizing the 
port traffic scheduling strategy, such as berth scheduling [ 7 ], berth and 
quay crane (B-QC) joint scheduling [ 8 ], yard crane scheduling [ 9 ], 
transfer vehicle scheduling [ 10 ], water-rail joint scheduling [ 11 ]. 
However, the primary purpose of traditional port traffic scheduling 
management is to achieve logistics optimization. Most studies did not 
consider the coupling relationship between logistics and energy con -
sumption, resulting in limited improvement of energy efficiency and 
carbon emissions in port areas. 
Replacing traditional energy with clean energy is another effective 
way to reduce port carbon emissions [ 12 – 15 ]. The coordinated method 
of ESSs is the key to clean energy consumption in ports. In [ 12 ], to 
improve the energy efficiency of ports, a two-stage sequential sched -
uling method for ports was proposed. The first stage was to optimize the

high-energy density ESSs. A coordinated strategy for port energy con -
sumption was proposed to improve port operational performance. 
However, Ref. [ 12 , 13 ] did not consider changing port loads through 
traffic scheduling. That is, they did not consider the “ transport-energy ” 
coupling characteristics of ports to address the clean energy consump -
tion. Some studies achieve load coordination through special means. In 
[ 14 ], a hierarchical structure of multi agent systems was proposed to 
achieve real-time control of port flexible loads to promote the con -
sumption of renewable energy in ports. Some studies focused on 
hydrogen consumption in ports. In [ 15 ], based on port logistic activities, 
a life cycle assessment and total cost of ownership (TCO) model of 
hydrogen fuel vehicles in ports was formulated, and the energy, eco -
nomic and environmental performance of hydrogen utilization under 
various green hydrogen and gray hydrogen in ports is further discussed. 
However, it only discussed the hydrogen energy consumption of mobile 
equipment in ports, and the energy coordination in the process of 
hydrogen production from electricity in ports was not considered. At 
present, most studies on clean energy consumption in ports only 
consider the coordination methods of power load, hydrogen load, cold 
or heat load, and rarely consider coordinating energy imbalance through 
the transferability characteristics of multiple energy loads in ports. That 
is, demand side management of loads can be realized by considering the 
coupling characteristics of “ transportation- energy ” in ports. With the 
update and development of port equipment, port equipment equipped 
with clean energy will dominate energy consumption in ports. Joint 
consideration of the port transportation and energy will have a signifi -
cant optimization potential in improving energy efficiency and reducing 
carbon emissions. However, there are few studies involving this aspect. 
Due to the high capital cost and limited lifetime of ESSs, reasonable 
capacity allocation of ESSs is another key issue to coordinate the 
imbalance of energy consumption economically and efficiently in ports. 
In [ 5 ], 17 possible renewable energy and ESSs solutions for seaports 
were evaluated through energy levelization cost and environment cost 
to determine the capacity and operation strategy of a near-zero carbon 
port. However, the enumeration method used in this study only verifies 
the effectiveness of the hybrid renewable energy system, which is 
difficult to achieve optimal performance. In [ 16 ], to address the optimal 
allocation and operation of renewable energy and ESS in ports, a two- 
stage optimization model was established to optimize the investment 
and operation cost of the system. However, it did not consider the effect 
of the actual operation strategy on the system capacity in the capacity 
optimization stage. In [ 17 ], to provide energy for the cold ironing sys -
tem locally, a capacity method for PV plants and ESSs in ports was 
proposed with the goal of optimizing annualized life cycle cost of ports. 
However, it only considers the cold ironing, without considering other 
key electrical and hydrogen loads in ports. In [ 18 ], a hybrid energy 
storage capacity allocation method was proposed to coordinate electric/ 
hydrogen load in ports with the goal of optimizing daily operating cost. 
However, it only considered the daily operation cost of ports for 
configuration, and did not consider the life cycle cost of the port. In 
addition, changes in the port's electricity/hydrogen load were not 
considered. In the issue of ESS coordinating energy consumption in 
seaports, the capacity configuration of ESS is related to various aspects 
of seaports, such as scales of seaport, operation modes, and operational 
strategies. At present, there is not much research on the allocation of ESS 
capacity in port renewable energy consumption. Few studies have 
considered both economic and environmental costs to optimize the 
configuration of ESSs. Furthermore, due to the mutual influence and 
constraints between ESS operation strategy and capacity configuration, 
if the two can be combined to design the capacity configuration of ESS, 
the results obtained will be more efficient. 
To promote the consumption of renewable energy and reduce carbon 
emissions in ports, in this paper, considering the coupling characteristics 
of transportation and energy, a multi-energy load model of ports is 
formulated. Furthermore, due to the mutual influence and constraint 
between the operation strategy and capacity configuration of ESSs, a 
hybrid energy storage system (HESS) energy management and capacity 
configuration method considering the hydrogen/ electricity load char -
acteristics of ports is proposed. The proposed method optimizes the 
capacity configuration and operation strategy of HESS by a nested bi- 
layer model, and improves the solution performance by an improved 
metamodel - based solution algorithm. The main contributions of this 
paper are as follows. 
- A daily electric load model and a daily hydrogen load model are 
presented based on the coupling characteristics of “ transportation - 
energy ” of ports to realize the demand-side management of multi energy 
load of ports. 
- A day-ahead transportation and energy collaborative scheduling 
model considering carbon emission costs is proposed to realize the 
economic and low-carbon operation of ports. 
- A HESS capacity allocation model is proposed with the goal of 
minimizing the annual operational life cycle cost of ports, and an 
improved metamodel based solution algorithm is presented to improve 
solution performance. 
The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 introduces an 
overview of the proposed bi-layer model. Section 3 presents the HESS 
coordination strategy for port operation. The HESS capacity allocation 
model is formulated in Section 4 . Section 5 discusses the improved meta- 
model based solving algorithm. Section 6 focuses on the case study and 
discussion. Finally, the paper is summarized in Section 7 . 
2. Overview of the proposed method 
Container terminals with continuous berths are being studied in this 
study. Fig. 1 presents an overview of the port area study case. The multi- 
energy load in this paper mainly considers hydrogen load and electric 
load. According to the operation process of ports, in the container 
unloading stage, electric energy consumption of fixed logistics equip -
ment is mainly considered, such as cold ironing and quay cranes. In the 
stage of transportation to yards, hydrogen energy consumption is 
considered for mobile logistics equipment such as container trucks and 
RTGs, as it is more convenient to use hydrogen power for mobile 
equipment. 
In this paper, a HESS is composed of a power to hydrogen (P2H) 
equipment (electrolyzer (Elz) and hydrogen tank) and a Lithium-ion 
battery (LiB). The P2H equipment mainly coordinates the hydrogen 
load. Besides, due to the configuration of hydrogen tank, it also affects 
the real-time electrical power balance of ports. LiB not only coordinates 
the balance of renewable energy and electric load in ports but also

Since the hydrogen/electricity load variation of ports is directly

the berth time is shifted. The blue part shows the change in power load 
when both the berth time and the number of QCs change. According to 
Fig. 2 , the power imbalance between load and renewables is quite 
different under different B-QC scheduling results. In the stage of trans -
portation to yards, containers are simultaneously transported to yards 
when unloaded from vessels, thus the hydrogen consumption of mobile 
equipment is also affected by B-QC scheduling. As a result, a multi- 
energy load model based on traffic scheduling can be formulated to 
realize demand-side management of port loads, to better coordinate the 
multi energy imbalance in ports. 
The daily energy imbalance of hydrogen / electricity in ports can be 
mitigated through two methods, namely demand-side management of 
port energy and coordination of HESS. If the two can be considered 
together, that is, the demand-side management of port energy and the 
coordination of HESS are considered at the same time, the coordination 
performance of energy can be further improved, while also enhancing 
the performance and economy of HESS. 
The operation strategy and capacity allocation of HESS are mutually 
influenced and constrained. Therefore, a nested bi-layer HESS capacity 
allocation model is proposed, as shown in Fig. 3 . By iteratively opti -
mizing the upper layer and lower layer, the bi-layer model optimizes the 
HESS capacity and operating strategy. In the lower layer, considering 
the characteristics of hydrogen/electricity load in ports, a “ trans -
portation-energy ” collaborative scheduling model is formulated. Then, 
the operating parameters such as the lifetime of HESS and the operating 
costs of ports are obtained. In the upper layer, a capacity allocation 
model for HESS is formulated with the goal of minimizing the annual 
operational life cycle cost of ports. The upper layer and lower layer are 
iteratively optimized through the HESS capacity parameters and the 
operating parameters of ports. 
In addition, to avoid the problem of low solution accuracy or effi -
ciency caused by the huge computational cost of traditional heuristic 
solution algorithms, an improved model-pursuing sampling (MPS) al -
gorithm is presented, which improves the accuracy of the solution at a 
low cost. 
3. Lower layer HESS coordination strategy 
The lower layer of the proposed method is the HESS coordination 
strategy. With the electrification / hydrogen power of port equipment, 
traditional port traffic scheduling also affects the port energy con -
sumption. Therefore, a hydrogen / electricity load model can be 
formulated combined with the traffic scheduling to realize demand-side 
management of the hydrogen/electricity load in ports.

5. Improved solution method of upper layer model 
In HESS bi-layer model, there are large number of variables in the 
lower layer and the calculation is intensive. The upper layer model is a 
multivariable nonlinear model. As a result, when solving the upper layer 
model, the traditional heuristic algorithm (such as particle swarm 
optimization, PSO) needs to call a large number of iterative calculations 
of the lower layer. There is a huge computational consumption problem, 
which is easy to lead to low accuracy or low efficiency. The mode- 
pursuing sampling (MPS) algorithm [ 21 ] based on meta-model can 
reduce the call of the lower layer by constructing a meta-model, which is 
an effective method to solve the computationally intensive black-box 
problem. 
The key of the meta model-based algorithm is to construct a math -
ematical model similar to the source model through a special sampling 
method, so as to replace the original complex model. It improves solving 
efficiency by reducing the number of expensive calculations used for 
evaluation. The schematic diagram of the meta model-based method is 
shown in Fig. 4 . The metamodel based optimization algorithms is 
particularly suitable for computationally intensive black-box optimiza -
tion problems and is an effective way to improve design efficiency 
[ 21 , 22 ]. 
The metamodel based MPS algorithm was proposed by G.Gary Wang 
in 2004. It uses mode-pursuing sampling method to generate more 
sample points in areas where the source model is more likely to have a 
minimum point. Then, radial basis function (RBF) is used to determine 
the region of the global optimal solution, and a quadratic polynomial 
response surface model (RSM) is constructed to determine global 
convergence.

6. Case study 
To verify the effectiveness of the proposed coordination strategy and 
capacity allocation method of HESS, historical data from Ningbo Port, 
China was used for simulation. The proposed strategy and models are 
implemented through MATLAB optimization toolbox and CPLEX 
toolbox. The lower layer collaborative scheduling model can be solved 
by the CPLEX optimization toolbox. The simulation parameter settings 
[ 23 , 24 ] are shown in Table I . 
A. Results of collaborative scheduling of “ transportation-energy ” in 
lower layer 
To verify the effectiveness of the multi energy supply and demand 
imbalance coordination strategy in the lower layer, a fixed capacity 
(empirical capacity) of LiB and Elz were used for simulation. The 
method for determining HESS empirical capacity is shown in previous 
research of authors [ 19 ]. The berth demand information for a typical 
day in the port area are shown in Table A2 in the Appendix. At the same 
time, the “ transportation-energy ” conventional scheduling (CS) method 
was simulated for comparison [ 12 ]. CS method, that is, according to the 
traditional operation process of ports to complete the transportation 
scheduling and energy scheduling. First, the B-QC scheduling is imple -
mented with the minimum total berth time, and then the yard sched -
uling is carried out with the goal of shortest transportation distance. 
Finally, the HESS coordination method proposed in this paper is used to 
achieve the energy scheduling. Fig. A3 in the Appendix shows the traffic 
scheduling results under the proposed collaborative scheduling (simul -
taneous scheduling, SS) method and CS method. Fig. 7 shows the day- 
ahead energy scheduling results under the two methods. Table II 
shows the comparison results of various methods. 
According to Fig. A3, Fig. 7 and Table II , both methods can meet the 
basic requirements of port traffic scheduling, such as intraday berths, no 
conflict between time and space, and reasonable distribution of QCs. 
However, the port operation has a better performance in multiple as -
pects under the SS method. In terms of energy consumption in ports, 
considering the coupling characteristics of “ transportation ” and “ en -
ergy ” , the traffic scheduling results under the SS method integrate the 
energy consumption caused by berth location, QC quantity, and yard 
location. Compared with CS method, the B-QC scheduling results under 
SS method are more concentrated in terms of berth location and berth 
time. It reduces the electrical / hydrogen load fluctuations in ports, 
while reducing its peak energy consumption, thereby reducing the 
power fluctuations that HESS needs to coordinate. Although the SS 
method increases the total berthing time, the total daily power demand 
in the ports is reduced by 11.9 % compare to CS method. In addition, the 
total distance transported by the container truck is reduced by 18.6 %, 
thus reducing the total hydrogen consumption in ports in a day. The 
change in hydrogen/electricity load in the port area also verifies the goal 
of multi-energy load-side management through “ transportation-energy ” 
collaborative scheduling. 
In terms of HESS coordinating the supply and demand imbalance of 
hydrogen/electricity in ports, as shown in Fig. 7 d, the change in SOC 
under SS method is greater than that under CS method. It indicates that 
the imbalance between energy supply and demand under SS method is 
more reliant on LiB for coordination, which also leads to a 17.1 % in -
crease in the daily cost of LiB. Although the berth cost (increased by USD 
153) and LiB cost (increased by USD 487) are increased under SS 
method, the dependence on the main grid is reduced. As a result, the 
main grid cost under SS method is only 28.6 % (reduced by USD 1053) of 
that under CS method, thus reducing the total operation cost by 7.2 % 
compared with CS method. In the lower layer, the transportation and 
energy are combined to optimize the operation of the port area. It not 
only reduces the operation cost but also reduces the power disturbance 
to the main grid, which can effectively promote the consumption of 
renewable energy in ports. 
Further, in terms of carbon emissions in ports, the day-ahead 
scheduling considers both the operation costs and the environmental 
costs. The cost function (19) includes the carbon emission costs of port 
transportation scheduling and energy scheduling. Under the SS method, 
the energy autonomy performance of the port area is better, which 
significantly reduces the carbon emissions of the main grid. Although it 
increases carbon emissions during berthing, the total carbon emissions 
of the port area are 35 % lower than those of CS method. In addition, to 
balance the multi-energy imbalance in ports, both SS method and CS 
method have significantly improved the economic and carbon emission 
performance compared with using only the main grid.

7. Conclusions 
To promote the renewable consumption and economic operation of 
ports, a HESS energy management and capacity allocation method is 
proposed based on the “ transportation-energy ” coupling characteristics 
of ports to coordinate the imbalance of hydrogen/electricity supply and 
demand in ports. The proposed method optimizes the energy manage -
ment strategy and capacity allocation of HESS through a nested bi-layer 
model. In the lower layer HESS energy management, a multi-energy load 
model based on port traffic scheduling is formulated to realize the 
demand-side management of port multi-energy load. Furthermore, 
considering the economic operation costs and environmental costs of 
ports, a “ transportation-energy ” collaborative scheduling model for 
HESS coordination is proposed. In the upper layer, a capacity allocation 
model for HESS is formulated with the goal of minimizing the annual 
operational life cycle cost of ports. To consider the mutual impact of 
HESS operation strategy and capacity configuration, the upper layer and 
the lower layer iteratively optimize each other through capacity pa -
rameters and operational parameters. Finally, to improve the accuracy 
and efficiency of the model solution, an improved MPS algorithm is 
presented. The simulation results based on historical data show that 
compared with the traditional port scheduling method, the proposed 
collaborative scheduling method with fixed HESS capacity reduces the 
daily operating cost and carbon emissions of ports by 7.2 % and 35 %, 
respectively. The annual cost and daily carbon emission of the proposed 
scheduling method are reduced by 8.2 % and 16.3 %, respectively under 
the optimal HESS capacity compared with the empirical capacity. At the 
same time, the annual cost of the improved MPS algorithm is reduced by 
USD 31,044 and USD 77,463 respectively compared with the standard 
MPS algorithm and PSO algorithm.
